patch.objective: Data durability and availability: replication, versioning, backups

sources.cite: AWS Certified Solutions Architect - Associate (SAA-C03) exam guide: Design secure architectures 30%, Design resilient architectures 26%, Design high-performing architectures 24%, Design cost-optimized architectures 20%
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch of the exam guide PDF on 2026-11-16. Relevant skills: Task 1.1 'Applying AWS security best practices to IAM users and root users (for example, multi-factor authentication [MFA])'; Task 1.3 'Implementing data backups and replications'; Task 2.2 'Implementing strategies to ensure the durability and availability of data (for example, backups)'.

sources.cite: Amazon RDS User Guide: Restoring a DB instance to a specified time
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-14 (no last-updated date shown). Relevant text: 'You can restore a DB instance to a specific point in time, creating a new DB instance without modifying the source DB instance'; 'RDS uploads transaction logs for DB instances to Amazon S3 every five minutes'; LatestRestorableTime is read with describe-db-instances; 'You can restore to any point in time within your backup retention period'; on restore 'you can choose the default virtual private cloud (VPC) security group. Or you can apply a custom VPC security group'; 'Restored DB instances are automatically associated with the default DB parameter and option groups.' The page does not say how long a restore takes; the scenario's 30 minutes is authored.
